title: ‘Cheap travel is not a defence’: the parents facing court for school absences in England

paragraphs.en: As the long school summer break approached its mid-point recently, Margate beach was crowded with families enjoying the brief reprieve between the year’s fourth and fifth heatwaves. For most, thoughts of the classroom were probably not at the forefront of their minds.
paragraphs.zh: 在漫长的暑假接近中点之时，最近马盖特（Margate）海滩上挤满了带着家人、享受今年第四次与第五次热浪之间短暂喘息的家庭。对大多数人来说，课堂大概并没有占据他们脑海的首要位置。

paragraphs.en: But for the seven mothers and two fathers who were summoned at 10am to a stuffy room in the town’s magistrates court, set just behind the beachfront strip of arcades, the subject was unavoidable. They were among hundreds of parents due in courts across England this month for failing to ensure their children had regularly attended school over the course of the last academic year.
paragraphs.zh: 但对于七位母亲和两位父亲来说，这个话题却无法回避——他们上午 10 点被传唤到小镇治安法庭（magistrates court）一间闷热的房间里，法庭就坐落在海滨拱廊游乐区后方的街道上。他们是本月将在英格兰各地法院出庭的数百名家长中的一部分，这些家长因未确保子女在上一学年经常到校上课而面临审理。

paragraphs.en: They faced fines, or in extreme cases the theoretical possibility of three months in prison, depending on the reasons provided for the absences.
paragraphs.zh: 根据缺课原因的不同，他们可能面临罚款，或者在极端情况下理论上可能被判入狱三个月。

paragraphs.en: The first defendant to be called in admitted that he had travelled abroad with his partner and daughter for 10 days at the start of the summer term. Taking her out of school to go on holiday for the third time in three consecutive years had pushed her annual attendance rate below 75%.
paragraphs.zh: 第一个被传唤的被告承认，他在夏季学期开学时与伴侣和女儿出国旅行了 10 天。连续三年里第三次在学期内带孩子去度假，使孩子的年出勤率降到了 75% 以下。

paragraphs.en: But the family had needed a break, he told the court, because two close friends had recently died, and the child’s mother had been unwell. The timing of the trip – immediately after rather than during the Easter holidays – was, he said, prompted by the strain the family had been under, rather than because travel was cheaper during term time.
paragraphs.zh: 但他告诉法庭，家人需要休息一下，因为两位亲近的朋友最近去世，孩子的母亲也一直身体不适。他说，选择在复活节假期刚结束之后而不是假期期间出行，是因为家人承受的压力所致，而不是因为学期中出行旅行更便宜。

paragraphs.en: “There’s a lot going on at home,” he told the court, in weary explanation.
paragraphs.zh: “家里发生了很多事情，”他用疲惫的语气向法庭解释道。

paragraphs.en: The three magistrates presiding over court two represented the sharp end of an ongoing drive to try to improve school attendance rates in England, which have never fully recovered after the closure of schools during Covid. Parents can be taken to court as a last resort if gentler attempts by the local authority to help them improve persistently poor attendance have failed, or if they have received multiple penalty notices for their child’s non-attendance within three years.
paragraphs.zh: 主持第二法庭的三位治安法官，代表了当前改善英格兰学校出勤率行动的最前沿。自新冠疫情期间学校关闭以来，英格兰的出勤率从未完全恢复。如果地方当局为帮助他们改善持续糟糕的出勤状况而采取的温和措施未能奏效，或者家长在三年内因孩子缺课收到多张罚款通知，那么把家长告上法庭是最后的手段。

paragraphs.en: It is a drive that is faltering. In the same week in London, the Department for Education released data showing the overall absence rate for the academic year 2025-26 for pupils in England was running at 6.93%, a slight rise on the previous year, and still significantly above the 2018-19 pre-Covid levels when the national overall absence rate in England was just 4.7%. Persistent absence rates have doubled since the pandemic, with nearly one in five children now missing at least 10% of school.
paragraphs.zh: 这是一项步履维艰的行动。同一周，伦敦的英国教育部（Department for Education）公布的数据显示，英格兰学生在 2025-26 学年的总体缺勤率为 6.93%，比上一年略有上升，仍显著高于疫情前 2018-19 学年英格兰全国总体缺勤率仅为 4.7% 的水平。自疫情以来，长期缺勤率翻了一番，如今近五分之一的儿童缺课至少 10%。
